tb21_profile.skill: Author one precise Python regex that encodes numeric range constraints (IPv4 octets 0-255 no leading zeros, month/day bounds), matches only the last date on qualifying lines, and rejects near-miss false positives via boundary/lookaround anchoring
tb21_profile.domain: Python re engine (alternation, backreferences, lookaround, word boundaries, MULTILINE, findall), IPv4 and YYYY-MM-DD text formats, log parsing
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec, single-artifact: write a regex to a file, graded by exact accept/reject behaviour over a corpus with adversarial near-matches

notes: This task is unusually pure: author ONE Python regex, no code, graded by re.findall behaviour over a corpus with adversarial near-matches. So skill (precise pattern authoring, false-positive control) and domain (regex + IPv4/date formats) dominate; task_form penalises the SWE bug-fix corpora as expected. The RTS/TW phone/email single-regex-with-backreference family is the best structural match anywhere and I ranked it high despite low lexical overlap in the shortlist. TMax's true strengths (WAF-evasion regex, IPv4 validation, clean/evil corpus matchers) came from my own searches, not the shortlist, which was dominated by generic log-ETL pipeline tasks that only share the word 'log'. No corpus is short of 10 defensible candidates here, though SWE-Smith/Rebench necessarily lose on task_form. Merge step: the phone/email RTS regex tasks recur across regex-chess and regex-log; they are genuinely on-point for regex authoring but are near-duplicates of each other, so treat multiple appearances as one signal.
